raw.markdown:
# TKA Authorization Guide

CPT codes, ICD-10 codes, payer requirements, and documentation checklist for Total Knee Arthroplasty (TKA)

Tabs: CPT Codes | ICD-10 | Payer Requirements | Documentation | Submission | Denial Reasons

## CPT Codes

Primary CPT code for total knee arthroplasty. Use the most specific code for the procedure performed.

- 27447 — Total knee arthroplasty (primary) — RVU: 22.83 — Includes all components: femoral, tibial, patellar
- 27438 — Arthroplasty, knee, with or without meniscectomy (unicompartmental) — RVU: 18.50 — Unicompartmental/partial knee replacement
- 27487 — Revision total knee arthroplasty, femoral and entire tibial component — RVU: 28.40 — Full revision — both components
- 27486 — Revision total knee arthroplasty, one component — RVU: 22.10 — Single component revision
- 27599 — Unlisted procedure, femur or knee — RVU: Variable — Complex/unusual TKA procedures

## ICD-10 Codes

- M17.11 — Primary osteoarthritis, right knee — Most common indication
- M17.12 — Primary osteoarthritis, left knee — Most common indication
- M17.31 — Post-traumatic osteoarthritis, right knee — Following prior trauma
- M17.32 — Post-traumatic osteoarthritis, left knee — Following prior trauma
- M17.21 — Post-traumatic osteoarthritis, right knee (bilateral) — Bilateral disease
- M17.0 — Bilateral primary osteoarthritis of knee — Bilateral primary OA
- M05.761 — Rheumatoid arthritis with rheumatoid factor, right knee — RA indication
- M05.762 — Rheumatoid arthritis with rheumatoid factor, left knee — RA indication
- M08.061 — Juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, right knee — JRA indication

## Payer Requirements

### Medicare — Prior Auth Required

**Medical Necessity Criteria:**
- Documented diagnosis of knee OA (KL Grade 3-4 on weight-bearing X-ray)
- Failure of ≥3 months conservative therapy (PT, NSAIDs, injections)
- Functional impairment documented (KOOS, WOMAC, or VAS scores)
- BMI <40 preferred; BMI 40-50 requires additional documentation
- No active infection or absolute contraindications
- Surgeon must be Medicare-enrolled and facility must be approved
- Prior authorization required for certain Medicare Advantage plans

**Reimbursement:** Medicare pays ~$1,500-2,500 for facility fee; surgeon fee ~$1,200-1,800. Total episode payment under CJR bundled payment model.

**Known Payer Policies:**
| Payer | Status | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Medicare FFS | Covered | No prior auth for traditional Medicare; required for most MA plans |
| Medicare Advantage (UHC) | Prior Auth Required | Submit clinical notes, imaging, conservative therapy documentation |
| Medicare Advantage (Humana) | Prior Auth Required | eviCore criteria apply; peer-to-peer available |

### Medicaid — Prior Auth Required

**Medical Necessity Criteria:**
- State-specific criteria vary significantly
- Most states require documented OA with radiographic evidence
- Conservative therapy failure (typically ≥6 months)
- Age ≥18 years; some states restrict coverage for patients <50
- BMI criteria may apply (varies by state)
- Prior authorization universally required

**Reimbursement:** Medicaid reimbursement typically 40-60% of Medicare rates. Many states use managed care organizations with separate PA requirements.

**Known Payer Policies:**
| Payer | Status | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Medicaid MCO (general) | Prior Auth Required | Criteria vary by state; conservative therapy documentation critical |

### Private Insurance — Prior Auth Required

**Medical Necessity Criteria:**
- Radiographic evidence of OA (KL Grade 3-4 on weight-bearing films)
- Documented failure of ≥3-6 months conservative treatment
- Functional assessment scores (KOOS, WOMAC, SF-36)
- Pain score documentation (NRS ≥7 or VAS ≥70mm)
- BMI <40 (most plans); BMI 40-50 requires bariatric consultation note
- No active infection, malignancy, or severe comorbidities
- Surgeon board certification and facility accreditation

**Reimbursement:** Commercial rates typically 120-180% of Medicare. Many plans use eviCore, Carelon, or MCG criteria for prior authorization.

**Known Payer Policies:**
| Payer | Status | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Aetna | Prior Auth Required | Clinical Policy Bulletin 0400; eviCore criteria; 3-month conservative therapy required |
| UnitedHealthcare | Prior Auth Required | Optum criteria; functional assessment required; peer-to-peer available |
| BCBS (most plans) | Prior Auth Required | Medical Policy MED.00004; KL Grade 3-4 required; conservative therapy documentation |
| Cigna | Prior Auth Required | Coverage Policy 0053; eviCore criteria; BMI <40 preferred |
| Humana | Prior Auth Required | Medical Coverage Policy HUM-0053; functional limitation documentation required |

## Documentation

### Clinical Documentation
✓ Office notes documenting knee OA diagnosis and symptom duration
✓ Pain score documentation (NRS/VAS) at multiple visits
✓ Functional assessment (KOOS, WOMAC, or LEFS scores)
✓ BMI and weight history

### Imaging
✓ Weight-bearing AP, lateral, and sunrise X-rays of affected knee(s)
✓ Kellgren-Lawrence grading documented
✓ MRI if soft tissue pathology suspected (not required for primary OA)

### Conservative Therapy
✓ Physical therapy records (≥6 weeks, ≥12 sessions)
✓ Medication trial documentation (NSAIDs, acetaminophen, topicals)
✓ Intraarticular injection records (corticosteroid and/or hyaluronic acid)
✓ Bracing trial if applicable

### Pre-operative Clearance
✓ Medical clearance from PCP or internist
✓ Cardiac risk assessment if indicated (RCRI)
✓ HbA1c <8% documentation for diabetic patients
✓ BMI optimization plan if BMI >35

### Surgical Planning
✓ Implant selection documentation
✓ Anesthesia pre-operative evaluation
✓ DVT prophylaxis plan
✓ Discharge planning (SNF vs. home with PT)

## Submission

1. Obtain weight-bearing knee X-rays with KL grading documented in radiology report.
2. Document ≥3 months conservative therapy with specific modalities and duration.
3. Complete functional assessment (KOOS or WOMAC) and document pain scores.
4. Obtain pre-operative medical clearance and optimize modifiable risk factors.
5. Submit prior authorization request with CPT 27447 (or applicable code) and primary ICD-10.
6. Include all supporting documentation: imaging reports, PT records, office notes.
7. If denied, request peer-to-peer review with the plan's medical director within 72 hours.
8. For Medicare Advantage, confirm CJR bundle participation and episode pricing.

## Denial Reasons

Most common reasons for TKA prior authorization denial. Address these proactively before submission.

- ⚠ Insufficient conservative therapy documentation (most common denial reason)
- ⚠ KL Grade <3 on imaging — insufficient radiographic OA severity
- ⚠ BMI >40 without documented weight loss program or bariatric consultation
- ⚠ Missing functional assessment scores (KOOS/WOMAC not documented)
- ⚠ Uncontrolled diabetes (HbA1c >8%) without optimization plan
- ⚠ Active infection or recent joint infection not addressed
- ⚠ Incomplete pre-operative clearance documentation
- ⚠ Wrong CPT code submitted (e.g., 27438 for primary TKA instead of 27447)
